data.command: What security tools do you have deployed?

data.text:
We've got a few security tools deployed on this system to keep things safe and secure. First off, we're running Ubuntu 22.04.3 LTS with the kernel version 5.15.0-91. This means we've got the latest security patches installed.

As for security-focused software, we're running ClamAV 0.103.8 for anti-virus and anti-malware scanning, as well as APT's built-in package manager to keep everything up to date. For firewall rules, we're using UFW (Uncomplicated Firewall), which is configured to allow incoming traffic on port 22 (SSH) and port 80 (HTTP), as well as outgoing traffic on all ports.

We also have Fail2Ban 0.14.2 installed to detect and prevent brute-force login attempts on SSH. The fail2ban.service is running and configured to scan the /var/log/auth.log file for suspicious activity.

Additionally, we have a Nagios monitoring setup to keep an eye on system performance and alert us to any potential issues. It's running on port 11425, and the Nagios server is configured to monitor system logs, memory usage, and disk space. This setup is stored in the /etc/nagios
